title: Audit Trail Generator for LLM Deployments

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: a prototype demonstrates feasibility of governance infrastructure, but real-world adoption and integration remain uncertain. Impact depends on ecosystem uptake.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Accessible: wrapping API calls, logging metadata (model version, timestamps, hashes), and generating structured reports are basic Python tasks well within beginner capabilities.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: a Python library with clear API wrapping, logging, and report generation functionality. Bounded scope with concrete output artifact.

novelty.reasoning: This idea has been directly implemented. 'Audit Trails for Accountability in Large Language Models' (arXiv:2601.20727, January 2026) presents a reference architecture and open-source Python library (`llm-audit-trail`) that implements exactly this: low-friction capture of lifecycle events, tamper-evident integrity via hash chaining, and recording of human governance decisions alongside technical telemetry. AuditableLLM (MDPI Electronics, 2025) provides a hash-chain-backed compliance-aware auditable framework. Additionally, 'Operationalizing LLM Governance in Enterprise Systems' (ResearchGate, 2026) covers monitoring, audit trails, and policy enforcement pipelines. The three-pillar governance architecture described in the literature directly subsumes this idea.
